question.problem: Consider the equivalence relation $∼$ on the set $A={0,1,2,…,9},$ defined by $a∼b$ if $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi a)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi b).$ How many distinct equivalence classes does $∼$ partition $A$ into?
question.worked_solution:
The equivalence classes of $∼$ partition $A,$ meaning that any element $a\in A$ belongs to exactly one distinct equivalence class.

So, we compute equivalence classes until all the elements of $A$ have been placed into an equivalence class.

$$
\begin{aligned}[0] & ={a\in A∣a∼0} \\  & ={a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi a)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi \cdot 0)} \\  & ={a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi a)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)} \\  & ={a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi a)=1} \\  & ={0,2,4,6,8} \\  \\ [1] & ={a\in A∣a∼1} \\  & ={a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi a)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi \cdot 1)} \\  & ={a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi a)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )} \\  & ={a\in A∣\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi a)=-1} \\  & ={1,3,5,7,9} \\ \end{aligned}
$$

All of the elements of $A$ have been placed into an equivalence class, so we are done.

We have $2$ distinct equivalence classes:

$$
[0]={0,2,4,6,8},\,[1]={1,3,5,7,9}.
$$
